name: GPT-4o
description: OpenAI's most advanced multimodal model, capable of processing text, images, and audio. Offers GPT-4-level intelligence with significantly faster response times and lower cost, making it suitable for production AI governance applications.
key_capabilities: 128K context window for large document processing
JSON mode for reliable structured responses
pros: Best price-to-performance ratio in the GPT-4 family
Multimodal capabilities enable document and image analysis workflows
Fast inference speed suitable for interactive applications
Strong function calling for agent tool use
Available via Azure OpenAI Service for enterprise compliance
cons: Requires API key management and usage monitoring
Data processing policies require review for regulated industries
Model behavior can vary between versions without notice
Limited availability in some regions without Azure OpenAI
Cost can scale quickly with high-volume usage
compliance_notes: Available through Azure OpenAI Service with enterprise data privacy guarantees (data not used for training). When accessed via OpenAI API directly, review data usage policies for compliance. Supports content filtering and abuse monitoring. SOC 2 Type 2 certified (OpenAI).
cost_per_token: $2.50 per 1M input tokens / $10.00 per 1M output tokens

name: GPT-4 Turbo
description: High-capability language model with 128K context window and knowledge cutoff of April 2024. Optimized for complex reasoning tasks, code generation, and detailed analysis with improved instruction following.
key_capabilities: 128K context window for large document analysis
Advanced reasoning and multi-step problem solving
Function calling with parallel tool use
Improved instruction following and reduced hallucination
pros: Excellent reasoning capabilities for complex governance analysis
Large context window supports processing lengthy regulatory documents
Reliable function calling for agent architectures
Well-established model with extensive documentation and community support
Available via Azure OpenAI Service for enterprise deployments
cons: Higher cost per token compared to GPT-4o
Slower inference speed than GPT-4o
Being superseded by GPT-4o for most use cases
Same data privacy considerations as other OpenAI models
Rate limits can constrain high-throughput applications
compliance_notes: Available through Azure OpenAI Service with enterprise data privacy guarantees. OpenAI API access subject to data usage policies that should be reviewed for regulated workloads. Supports content filtering. SOC 2 Type 2 certified (OpenAI).
cost_per_token: $10.00 per 1M input tokens / $30.00 per 1M output tokens

name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
description: Anthropic's most capable model balancing intelligence and speed. Excels at complex reasoning, coding, and nuanced analysis tasks. Designed with constitutional AI principles for safer outputs.
key_capabilities: 200K context window for extensive document processing
Strong coding and technical writing capabilities
pros: Excellent at nuanced reasoning and following complex instructions
200K context window is largest among leading models
Strong safety alignment reduces harmful output risk
Available on AWS Bedrock and GCP Vertex AI for enterprise compliance
Competitive performance with lower hallucination rates on benchmarks
Good at structured output and consistent formatting
cons: Not available via Azure OpenAI Service
Anthropic API has fewer enterprise compliance certifications than Azure/AWS
Can be overly cautious in responses due to safety training
Smaller ecosystem of fine-tuning and customization options
Regional availability more limited than GPT models
compliance_notes: Available through AWS Bedrock (data stays in AWS account, inherits AWS compliance) and GCP Vertex AI. Anthropic is SOC 2 Type 2 certified. When accessed via Bedrock, data is not used for model training. Anthropic's data retention policies should be reviewed when using direct API access for regulated workloads.
cost_per_token: $3.00 per 1M input tokens / $15.00 per 1M output tokens

name: Gemini 1.5 Pro
description: Google's most capable model with an industry-leading 1M token context window. Built on Google's Mixture-of-Experts architecture, excelling at long-document understanding, multimodal reasoning, and code generation.
key_capabilities: Native Google Cloud integration via Vertex AI
pros: Largest context window enables processing entire codebases or regulatory documents
Strong multimodal capabilities for diverse input types
Competitive pricing especially for long-context workloads
Native integration with Google Cloud and Vertex AI
Good performance on reasoning and analysis benchmarks
cons: Only available through Google Cloud / Vertex AI for enterprise use
Fewer third-party platform integrations compared to OpenAI models
Google Cloud has fewer government-specific compliance offerings
Model versioning and deprecation policies less transparent
Smaller developer community and fewer production case studies
compliance_notes: Available through Google Cloud Vertex AI with enterprise data privacy controls. Data is not used for model training when accessed via Vertex AI. Google Cloud compliance certifications apply (SOC 1/2/3, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP). Assured Workloads can provide additional compliance guardrails.
cost_per_token: $1.25 per 1M input tokens (<=128K) / $5.00 per 1M output tokens

name: Llama 3.1 405B
description: Meta's largest open-weight language model with 405 billion parameters. Available for self-hosting or through cloud providers (AWS Bedrock, Azure, GCP). Offers strong performance with full control over data residency and model deployment.
key_capabilities: Open weights enabling self-hosting and customization
Function calling and tool use support
pros: Open weights provide full transparency and auditability
Self-hosting option gives complete data residency control
No per-token API costs when self-hosted (infrastructure costs only)
Can be fine-tuned for domain-specific governance tasks
Available on AWS Bedrock, Azure, and GCP for managed deployment
No vendor lock-in to a single API provider
cons: Self-hosting requires significant GPU infrastructure (8x A100/H100)
Managed cloud hosting still incurs per-token costs
Slightly lower performance than GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 on complex reasoning
Smaller 128K context window compared to Claude and Gemini
Community support rather than dedicated enterprise support
Responsible use license has some restrictions on deployment
compliance_notes: Open weights enable full audit of model behavior. Self-hosting provides complete data sovereignty with no data leaving organizational boundaries. When accessed via cloud providers (Bedrock, Azure, Vertex AI), inherits respective platform compliance certifications. Meta's Responsible Use Guide should be reviewed for deployment constraints.
cost_per_token: $0.00195 per 1K input tokens / $0.00256 per 1K output tokens (via AWS Bedrock)
